tEn: Dylan Field: Design Is the New Code and AI Is Democratizing Creativity
tZh: Dylan Field：设计即新代码，AI 正在让创造力民主化
sEn: Figma CEO Dylan Field on why design is becoming the new code as AI reshapes programming, and how creativity is being democratized.
sZh: Figma CEO Dylan Field 谈 AI 重塑编程时代为何设计成为新代码，以及创造力如何被民主化。

consensus.en: Design is the new code; as coding models improve, differentiation shifts to design, brand, and point of view.
consensus.zh: 设计是新的代码；随着编码模型进步，差异化转向设计、品牌和观点。

consensus.en: AI lowers the floor for production but does not raise the ceiling; humans raise the ceiling through bold creativity.
consensus.zh: AI 降低了生产门槛，但并未提高上限；人类通过大胆创造提高上限。

consensus.en: SaaS is not dead; specialized, user-obsessed software companies like Cursor can thrive despite frontier model competition.
consensus.zh: SaaS 没有死；像 Cursor 这样专注用户、高度专业化的软件公司能在前沿模型竞争中蓬勃发展。

consensus.en: Model progress is easily mistaken for product progress; building professional design tools requires years of workflow refinement.
consensus.zh: 模型进步容易被误认为产品进步；构建专业设计工具需要多年工作流打磨。

consensus.en: In the attention economy, only truly novel and bold work breaks through; AI-generated average output gets ignored.
consensus.zh: 在注意力经济中，只有真正新颖和大胆的作品才能突破；AI 生成的平均产出会被忽视。

consensus.en: Everyone can be a maker; AI should expand human potential, not replace human thinking.
consensus.zh: 每个人都可以成为创造者；AI 应扩展人类潜能，而非取代人类思考。

contrarian.en: AI is not raising the creative ceiling; that was wrong. Humans raise the ceiling, not AI.
contrarian.zh: AI 并未提高创造上限；那是错的。提高上限的是人类，不是 AI。

contrarian.en: The Adobe deal block was poor policy; 16-month reviews can destroy companies, as Roomba's bankruptcy shows.
contrarian.zh: 阻止 Adobe 交易是糟糕的政策；16 个月的审查可能摧毁公司，Roomba 破产就是例证。

contrarian.en: Claude Design was not an instant hit; making good design tools for professionals is genuinely hard.
contrarian.zh: Claude Design 并非一炮而红；为专业人士打造优秀设计工具确实很难。

contrarian.en: AI progress is incremental in creativity and design because these are non-verifiable domains, unlike math.
contrarian.zh: AI 在创造力和设计上的进步是渐进的，因为这些是不可验证的领域，与数学不同。

contrarian.en: People are letting AI think for them; that is the easy path, not the interesting one.
contrarian.zh: 人们正在让 AI 替自己思考；那是容易的路，不是有趣的路。

contrarian.en: It is okay to mourn the loss of mystery as AI solves famous math problems; we gain and lose something.
contrarian.zh: 当 AI 解决著名数学问题时，为失去神秘感而哀悼是正常的；我们有所得也有所失。

turns.zh: 就像你是回顾历史来定义市场，这可能是作为监管者唯一合乎逻辑的方式，还是你作为技术专家向前看？这在你怎么考虑市场规模方面可能非常不同，但总之，那是全员大会。实际上那是寒假的第一天，挺有趣的。所以我们告诉所有人：好，享受假期。我们在假期期间流量其实少得多，因为我们是工作产品。那天是周五，然后周末意识到，好，这要有个结论了。周一早上，给所有人发消息说：“嘿，中午全员大会。”想的话就拨进来，这是正在发生的事，这是完整的细节。所以，首先，公司那么多人出席了。看到出席率真是太棒了。你知道，真的是假期第一天。其次，我想说情绪是解脱，因为不是对摆脱 Adobe 的解脱，而是对不再有不确定性的解脱。那么长时间的不确定性真的很紧张。人们不得不在脑子里装两个世界，他们不完全确定未来会怎样。所以，那是当时的情绪。就是有点轻松了。然后从那里开始，是的，我认为你问的问题是对的。你如何确保每个人都全力以赴？我们做的方式是，我们说：“看，我就在公司 Slack 里发了个视频，给所有人发了邮件，说：‘嘿，如果你在非常努力地工作后累了，如果你是这段时间加入的，以为要去 Adobe 工作，而实际上创业公司不适合你，请知道，我们会非常努力地工作，拼命干，没有羞耻，我们仍然关系良好。如果你想离开，这里有几个月的薪水。欢迎你告诉我们，我们会让它超级容易。’”

turns.en: In a world of AI, agentic AI, I have this capacity to prompt as a human and say, "I want to make something that looks like, feels like, and does X." And this magical technology takes off and does it. And I end up with a product. Sometimes the product is great. Sometimes the product sucks. But it's improving the ability for these tools to do that. Historically, I would have needed a product manager, a designer, a bunch of engineers to do the actual building of the product, whether it's a software product or a hardware product. Increasingly, though, it seems like AI is doing more and more of those tools. Can you just give me your view on the future of human creativity in this era, this future era that we're waltzing into, the singularity we're falling into? Where does human creativity play a role? And where do the gaps still need to be filled for taking human creativity to the realization moment?
turns.zh: 在 AI、智能体式 AI 的世界里，作为人类，我有能力提示说：“我想做一个看起来、感觉起来、做起来像 X 的东西。”然后这项神奇的技术启动并完成它。我最终得到一个产品。有时产品很棒。有时产品很烂。但它正在提高这些工具做到这一点的能力。历史上，我需要一个产品经理、一个设计师、一群工程师来实际构建产品，无论是软件产品还是硬件产品。然而，越来越多地，AI 似乎在完成越来越多的这些工具。你能就这个时代、我们正步入的未来时代、我们正坠入的奇点中人类创造力的未来，给我你的看法吗？人类创造力在哪里发挥作用？在将人类创造力带到实现时刻的过程中，哪些差距仍然需要填补？

turns.en: It's the case, I think, that uh we're lowering the floor with AI, making it so that all of the production, whether it's code or it's uh motion, video, design, whatever you name it, uh if it's digital, you're lowering the floor to make it happen. Um everyone can be part of that and it's more democratized. Ironically, and I I used to believe uh even a few years ago I said it at our annual user conference Config, I said the ceiling will be raised by AI. You'll be able to do greater things before. That was wrong. Uh the ceiling has stayed the same. AI is not raising the ceiling. Humans are raising the ceiling, though.
turns.zh: 我认为情况是，呃，我们正在用 AI 降低门槛，使得所有的生产，无论是代码还是呃，动态、视频、设计，无论你说什么，呃，如果是数字的，你都在降低实现它的门槛。嗯，每个人都可以参与其中，它更加民主化。讽刺的是，我过去相信，甚至几年前我在我们的年度用户大会 Config 上说过，我说天花板会被 AI 提高。你以前能够做更伟大的事情。那是错的。呃，天花板保持不变。AI 没有提高天花板。不过，人类正在提高天花板。

turns.en: The creatives, the designers out there, when they choose to focus, invest their time, and to be bold, and try to do something no one else has ever done before, that's when we see the ceiling raised. And at that point it's a question of: do you care about being in the center of distribution? Do you care about a mean or average result? Is that sufficient for your task? Or do you need something that shows that you care, that you took the time to actually go make this thing? Do you need to go and be beyond what is the minimum bar? And in the world of software design and product, we're seeing exponentially more software than ever before. It's exactly what you'd predict. The exponential continues. You look at App Store numbers. The App Store numbers are exactly that same exponential. And we're seeing that the usage and utilization of apps flat. So, people are using just the same amount of apps, but the amount of apps that you can get, it's bigger than ever and growing. And I think it just speaks to, okay, there's a need to differentiate yourself if you're building any kind of software. Well, how do you do that? It's not code because anyone can create code now. That's not the hard part anymore. So, my view is design is the new code. It's the layer above. You have to make it so that your design is differentiated. And you have to have a point of view, and a good brand and marketing. And the point of view I think is the part that is probably missed the most.
turns.zh: 创意人士、设计师们，当他们选择专注、投入时间、大胆尝试去做别人从未做过的事情时，我们才能看到天花板被抬高。而到了那个节点，问题就变成了：你在意的是处于分布的中心吗？你在意的是平均或普通的结果吗？这对你的任务来说足够吗？还是你需要一些能表明你在意、你花了时间去真正做出这个东西的东西？你需要超越最低标准吗？在软件设计和产品领域，我们看到的软件数量呈指数级增长，比以往任何时候都多。这正是你会预测到的。指数增长在继续。你看看 App Store 的数据。App Store 的数据正是同样的指数增长。而我们看到应用的使用率和利用率却持平了。所以，人们使用的应用数量不变，但你能获取的应用数量却比以往任何时候都多，而且在增长。我认为这恰恰说明，如果你在构建任何类型的软件，就需要让自己与众不同。那么，如何做到呢？不是代码，因为现在任何人都能写代码。那不再是难的部分了。所以，我的观点是：设计是新的代码。它是更高的一层。你必须让你的设计与众不同。你必须有自己的观点，以及好的品牌和营销。而观点，我认为可能是最被忽视的部分。

turns.en: Is this also what human creativity is? If you're not doing something that's never been done before, you're not creating something, you're mimicking something, you're copying something, you're xeroxing something. But to do something new is to create. And newness requires doing things that have never been done before.
turns.zh: 这也是人类创造力的本质吗？如果你没有做从未做过的事情，你就不是在创造，而是在模仿、复制、复印。但做新的事情就是创造。而新意要求做从未做过的事情。

turns.en: By definition.
turns.zh: 从定义上讲。

turns.en: By definition.
turns.zh: 从定义上讲。

turns.en: And therefore you are operating outside of this distribution of training. It's not even about operating outside the mean of the distribution, which is where you start if you're just prompting without any kind of advanced scaffolding around it. But you're actually doing something that is breaking through and it's unique. And I do think that will be rewarded by the market. Everyone's going to see it. I think it's even rewarded by the attention market of organizations. I'm already hearing from so many like, 'Ugh, I got another deck made by AI today.'
turns.zh: 因此，你是在这个训练分布之外运作。甚至不是关于在分布均值之外运作，如果你只是提示而没有围绕它的任何高级脚手架，那就是你的起点。但你实际上在做一些突破性的、独特的事情。我确实认为这会得到市场的回报。每个人都会看到。我认为它甚至会得到组织的注意力市场的回报。我已经听到很多人说：‘唉，我今天又收到一份 AI 做的演示文稿。’

turns.en: Totally.
turns.zh: 完全同意。

turns.en: And I don't even know if the person who made it—I don't know if they wrote it. Do they even know what's in their deck? And at Figma we actually made it so that it was just a simple thing, but we said, 'Hey, if you are using AI in your writing of any kind, just put at the top written with AI.' Very simple, very easy to follow. And people made jokes about it internally, but people do it. And it makes it so that we can all trust that when we see something, we know that it's been cared for enough that it's worth your time to process. And I think that we're going to see some bifurcation here around trust. And one way to get trust is to do something with your hands. The other point that's important is if you have a vision or if you have a point of view in your head of how something should be designed or look aesthetically or from an experiential standpoint, I think it's great to start with building with AI. It gives you something to get past the blank page, blank canvas problem. You can then react to it and say, 'Here are all the things I don't like. I'm going to go fix these things. I'm going to change them up.' Because it's really helpful to have a back and forth. But if you have your own vision and you're trusting AI to implement it, you're doing it through the lens of AI. And AI has kind of its own distribution.
turns.zh: 我甚至不知道做这个的人——我不知道是不是他们写的。他们甚至知道自己的演示文稿里有什么吗？在 Figma，我们实际上做了一个简单的设置，我们说：‘嘿，如果你在任何写作中使用 AI，就在顶部写上“由 AI 撰写”。’非常简单，非常容易遵循。内部有人开玩笑，但人们确实这么做了。这样我们都能信任，当我们看到某个东西时，我们知道它被足够用心地对待，值得你花时间处理。我认为我们会在信任方面看到一些分化。获得信任的一种方式是用手做东西。另一个重要点是，如果你有愿景，或者你头脑中有关于某物应该如何设计、美学上或体验上应该是什么样子的观点，我认为从用 AI 构建开始很好。它让你越过空白页、空白画布的问题。然后你可以对它做出反应，说：‘这些是所有我不喜欢的东西。我要去修复这些。我要改变它们。’因为来回反复非常有帮助。但如果你有自己的愿景，却信任 AI 来实现它，你是在通过 AI 的镜头来做。而 AI 有它自己的分布。

turns.en: The model fit by it, yeah.
turns.zh: 模型拟合它，是的。

turns.en: Yeah. And so you're not going to get exactly what you want. Now, if you are able to do both, and that's what we're trying to enable in Figma, make code a material on the canvas, make it so that you can go start by building. You can build a thing if you like. But also when you want to think and work with your hands, you can do that, too.
turns.zh: 是的。所以你不会得到完全你想要的东西。现在，如果你能两者兼顾，这就是我们在 Figma 试图实现的：让代码成为画布上的一种材料，让你可以从构建开始。如果你愿意，你可以构建一个东西。但当你想要思考和动手工作时，你也可以这样做。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: Go back and forth rapidly.
turns.zh: 快速来回切换。

turns.en: Right. I remember the early days of Photoshop just having been an avid user from the early days. People freaked out when layers happened and then they freaked out when all the filters came out and when Kai's Power Tools came out and everyone was like, 'What's the role of the photographer anymore? It's like you're destroying the art of photography, the creativity of photography.' But it unleashed a new era of creativity because now these new artists emerged that could use these filters and use these layering tools and capabilities to reimagine what's possible on a canvas. And it was basically a new toolkit. It doesn't mean that the old creatives mapped perfectly to the new creative system and tools. But there was an explosion in creativity and human potential that arose from this and we pushed boundaries in all sorts of ways. Feels like we might be entering that era again.
turns.zh: 对。我记得 Photoshop 的早期，我从早期就是 avid 用户。图层出现时人们吓坏了，然后所有滤镜出来时、Kai's Power Tools 出来时，大家又说：‘摄影师的角色现在是什么？这像是在摧毁摄影艺术、摄影的创造力。’但它开启了一个新的创造力时代，因为现在出现了新的艺术家，他们可以使用这些滤镜、这些图层工具和能力来重新想象画布上的可能性。它基本上是一个新的工具包。这并不意味着旧的创意人士完美地映射到新的创意系统和工具。但由此产生了创造力和人类潜力的爆发，我们在各个方面推动了边界。感觉我们可能再次进入那个时代。

turns.en: I'm a big believer in that and I think that part of it is what I described about market dynamics. In order to get attention, in order to get engagement, in order to get people to care, you have to do something new.
turns.zh: 我对此深信不疑，我认为部分原因就是我描述的关于市场动态的内容。为了获得关注、参与度，为了让人们在意，你必须做一些新的事情。

turns.en: You have to actually be daring and try things that are bold. The resistance to change is real, and there's a great thing you can Google for your point. Look up the mailing list for when layers was introduced. And it's like people going, "This is the worst thing ever." You can find it. If you Google, it's on a mailing list that's publicly available. And you can see all the reactions.
turns.zh: 你必须真正敢于冒险，尝试大胆的事情。对变革的抵制是真实存在的，关于你的观点，有一件很棒的事你可以用谷歌搜到。查一下 layers 被引入时的邮件列表。人们会说：“这是史上最糟糕的东西。”你能找到。如果你谷歌一下，它就在一个公开可用的邮件列表上。你可以看到所有的反应。

turns.en: Totally.
turns.zh: 完全同意。

turns.en: But obviously it became the future. And I think that there are also still photographers in the world who are doing incredible work, but the bigger disruption, if we're going to be real, it was the camera phone. That was what made it so that people stopped buying cameras that were dedicated to the task of photography because the best camera is the one that's on you. And started treating photography in a different way with Instagram and their camera phone. So it transformed for a lot of people and I can't tell you if it's better or worse as a result. But there was change.
turns.zh: 但显然它成为了未来。我认为世界上仍然有摄影师在做着令人难以置信的工作，但更大的颠覆，如果我们说实话，是拍照手机。正是它让人们不再购买专门用于摄影的相机，因为最好的相机是随身携带的那个。人们开始用 Instagram 和拍照手机以不同的方式对待摄影。所以对很多人来说它发生了转变，我无法告诉你结果是好是坏。但确实发生了变化。

turns.en: There's one view on human creativity that human creativity is basically connecting dots in the unconscious that you've seen or experienced all of these things in your life or in your set of inputs, sensory inputs, and from those inputs you connect dots and then you extrapolate a forward view of things that hasn't perhaps been seen in the world before. Do you agree with that view on creativity and is it distinct from actually what AI does? And again, I want to go back to the uniqueness of the human in an AI era.
turns.zh: 有一种关于人类创造力的观点认为，人类创造力基本上是在无意识中连接点，你在生活中或在你的一组输入、感官输入中看到或经历过所有这些事情，从这些输入中你连接点，然后你推断出世界上可能从未见过的事物的前瞻性观点。你同意这种创造力观点吗？它与 AI 实际所做的有区别吗？而且，我想再次回到 AI 时代人类的独特性。

turns.en: Well, I think that one thing that happens with humans is they're always seeking novelty. Like our reward function is different than an AI's. Also our loss function. Like if I was to open this bottle of water and splashed all over you and you got mad at me, like you bet I'm not going to do that again. But an AI like, you know, with RL you got like really tell it a bunch of times that you know, you don't do that.
turns.zh: 嗯，我认为人类的一个特点是他们总是在寻求新奇。就像我们的奖励函数与 AI 的不同。我们的损失函数也不同。比如如果我打开这瓶水泼你一身，你对我发火，你赌我肯定不会再做一次。但 AI 呢，你知道，用强化学习你得真的告诉它很多次，你知道，不要那样做。

turns.en: Robot, stop kicking me.
turns.zh: 机器人，别踢我。

turns.en: Yeah, well, and maybe that'll change with architectures over time, but like overall the brain is different than the current systems that we've made with AI. And I think that it's unknown. We don't know much about neuroscience overall. I'd love to get to the point where we all know more about neuroscience, but something is fundamentally different there when it comes to creativity. And I also think design is different than creativity. It's not just creativity, it's also problem solving like I mentioned earlier. And the combination of the two is I just find it fascinating because you have a user, you're trying to solve their needs, you're trying to do so in a way that stands out as creative and it connects with them. And also, you have to connect to wider systems. The marketing and brand, the culture, the business problems, and so on, and holding all that in your head at different levels of abstraction while trying to deliver a screen or a flow that from a search space standpoint can be a combinatorial explosion is just pretty cool. It's pretty fascinating.
turns.zh: 是的，也许随着架构的演变，这种情况会改变，但总的来说，大脑与我们用 AI 创造的当前系统是不同的。我认为这是未知的。我们对神经科学整体了解不多。我希望我们能达到对神经科学了解更多的那一天，但在创造力方面，那里有根本性的不同。我还认为设计不同于创造力。它不仅仅是创造力，还是解决问题，就像我之前提到的。而两者的结合，我只是觉得它很迷人，因为你有一个用户，你试图解决他们的需求，你试图以一种脱颖而出、富有创意的方式做到这一点，并与他们产生联系。而且，你还必须连接到更广泛的系统。营销和品牌、文化、商业问题等等，并在不同的抽象层次上把所有这些都记在脑子里，同时试图交付一个屏幕或一个流程，从搜索空间的角度来看，这可能是一个组合爆炸，这真的很酷。非常迷人。

turns.en: I'm actually personally really excited about the idea of reinventing existing art form and media where AI can enable more dynamic generation, where the creator steps up a level, sets a bunch of parameters, but doesn't actually necessarily render the final product, but the final product, sort of like in a video game, is rendered on the fly with the user in front of it. But the creator, the creative team behind a video game, for example, is building all of the object. They're building the storyline. They're building the narrative flow. And the realization of that is much more dynamic, but I feel like it's going to find its way. It's going to leech its way into many more totally different media.
turns.zh: 我个人其实非常兴奋于重新发明现有艺术形式和媒体的想法，AI 可以实现更动态的生成，创作者提升一个层次，设置一堆参数，但不一定实际渲染最终产品，而最终产品，就像在电子游戏中一样，是在用户面前实时渲染的。但创作者，比如电子游戏背后的创意团队，正在构建所有对象。他们正在构建故事情节。他们正在构建叙事流程。而它的实现要动态得多，但我觉得它会找到自己的方式。它会渗透到许多完全不同的媒体中。

turns.en: We have products around that, too. Like in Figma design, you can have generative tools and shaders where you can do very much that. Or we have a product called Weave. And Weave is basically a node-based system. You can connect model outputs into other inputs and such. And the whole idea is like it's not bad to generate with AI, but you need a way to craft that clay. You need a way to mold it. And with Weave, people do like the most amazing video and photo work and overall just like the outcomes that are achievable with it are incredible. So yeah, I think that if you've got the intention, if you actually care to do the work, you can always get to a better result. And people, you know, new model drops, there's like this AI psychosis moment that people are in for a few days. And it's like, I think also aided by algo feeds, the best results rise to the top. Everyone's like, this model is everything. And then a few days later, it's okay, okay, I know the kind of like main tropes of the model. And you adapt fast. Like, the novelty's gone. It no longer is a thing that's kind of like rewarding you or firing off your dopamine system or whatever. And instead, you're like, okay, well, yeah, it always does that thing. How do I move past it? And that seems to be the continued loop we're in. Which is sort of fascinating because models keep getting so good when it comes to these formal domains, math, cybersecurity. Like the IQ points just stack and stack and stack. And then, for creativity and for design, it's very incremental progress overall. Maybe that will change at some point, but I think the fact that these are non-verifiable domains has something to do with it.
turns.zh: 我们也有围绕这个的产品。比如在 Figma 设计中，你可以有生成工具和着色器，你可以做很多那样的事情。或者我们有一个叫 Weave 的产品。Weave 基本上是一个基于节点的系统。你可以将模型输出连接到其他输入等等。整个想法是，用 AI 生成并不坏，但你需要一种方法来塑造那个黏土。你需要一种方法来塑造它。而用 Weave，人们做出最惊人的视频和照片作品，总的来说，用它可实现的结果是不可思议的。所以是的，我认为如果你有意图，如果你真的在乎做这项工作，你总能得到更好的结果。而人们，你知道，新模型发布时，人们会有几天的 AI 精神病时刻。而且我认为这也得益于算法推送，最好的结果会浮到顶部。每个人都觉得，这个模型就是一切。然后几天后，好吧好吧，我知道了模型的主要套路。你适应得很快。新奇感消失了。它不再是一种奖励你或激发你多巴胺系统的东西。相反，你会说，好吧，是的，它总是做那件事。我如何超越它？这似乎是我们所处的持续循环。这有点迷人，因为模型在形式领域，数学、网络安全方面越来越好。就像智商点数不断堆叠。然后，对于创造力和设计，整体进展非常渐进。也许某个时候会改变，但我认为这些是不可验证的领域这一事实与此有关。

turns.en: And it's probably the fact that maybe that is the human role in the AI toolkit, which is conceive, create, design, and let the AI do more of the work, but it gives you the ability to do much more work. Any art or media that you're particularly excited about or interested in that's kind of emerging right now?
turns.zh: 这可能是因为，也许这就是人类在 AI 工具包中的角色，即构思、创造、设计，让 AI 做更多的工作，但它让你有能力做更多的工作。你现在特别兴奋或感兴趣的任何艺术或媒体正在涌现吗？

turns.en: You know, I find it fascinating when people do sort of like new AI experiments. For example, it puts it in the media category. There was a designer artist type that made a webpage the other day, and it was like a letter to Figma, actually. So, it caught my attention cuz I was, you know, getting the Figma hit on the algo feed.
turns.zh: 你知道，当人们做新的 AI 实验时，我觉得很迷人。例如，把它归入媒体类别。前几天有一个设计师艺术家类型的人做了一个网页，实际上它像是一封给 Figma 的信。所以它引起了我的注意，因为你知道，我在算法推送中看到了 Figma 的热门内容。

turns.en: And every time you moved away from it, and came back, it got slightly more degraded. And it was basically a comment on attention. But thought that was really cool.
turns.zh: 每次你离开它，再回来，它就会稍微退化一点。它基本上是对注意力的一种评论。但我觉得那真的很酷。

turns.en: Oh, cool. That was a piece of art.
turns.zh: 哦，酷。那是一件艺术品。

turns.en: I thought so. It was a webpage.
turns.zh: 我也这么认为。那是一个网页。

turns.en: Yeah. But like I thought that the technique and the way that they went about it was really neat and like not something that many others have done. I've seen a few other things like that, but overall I thought it was a very cool way to do it. It was also just a very well-written letter. I liked the letter, too.
turns.zh: 是的。但我觉得他们的技巧和方式真的很巧妙，不是很多人做过的事情。我见过其他一些类似的东西，但总的来说，我认为这是一种非常酷的做法。它也是一封写得非常好的信。我也喜欢那封信。

turns.en: But yeah, I see stuff like this, and back in the day I remember seeing people do like NFT art with AI when NFTs were a thing, you know, so it's like 2019 or something like that. But the way they did it sometimes was really remarkable. I mean, Holly Herndon's work around taking her voice and making it so that her voice was something that people could use in an almost open-source way. That was quite incredible and ahead of its time. And I think this sort of play between what is me, what is the collective, and what is it that is unique and ownable versus what is not is quite fascinating. I've always been fascinated by that intersection.
turns.zh: 但没错，我见过类似的东西，我记得以前 NFT 还流行的时候，有人用 AI 做 NFT 艺术，大概是 2019 年左右。但他们有时做的方式真的很了不起。我是说，Holly Herndon 的作品，她把自己的声音变得几乎开源，让人们可以使用。那相当不可思议，而且超前于时代。我觉得这种在“什么是我、什么是集体、什么是独特且可拥有的、什么不是”之间的博弈非常迷人。我一直对那个交叉点很着迷。

turns.en: Yeah, that's cool. Just as we wrap up, a lot of the commentary on AI that's negative is that it takes away human agency, human potential gets capped out. Can you just talk a little bit about your view on the potential of every human to be a creative, to be a designer, and how AI might perhaps magnify every person, not just the quote creatives where they're in some elite class of artists in some special building, but the ability for every human to create and the ability for every human to design and produce things in the world, and where you sit with that right now.
turns.zh: 是的，那很酷。就在我们收尾的时候，很多关于 AI 的负面评论是说它剥夺了人的能动性，人的潜力被限制了。你能谈谈你对每个人都有潜力成为创作者、成为设计师的看法吗？以及 AI 可能如何放大每个人，不仅仅是那些所谓的创作者——他们属于某个精英艺术家阶层，在某个特殊建筑里——而是每个人创造的能力，每个人设计和生产世界上事物的能力，以及你现在对此的立场。

turns.en: I think it's even broader. I think it's as a human in general, pre-AI, post-AI, you have a choice. Do you want to consume or create? Do you want to take the easy path or do you want to climb the mountain? And what I'm seeing happen right now a lot is people are letting AI think for them. Less at Figma but more just in my interactions with the world, I just see a lot of this at the moment. And that's one path you can take, but the other one is actually use AI to further your understanding of the world, to learn, to do things you never would have dared to do before because they would have taken so much time to learn or it's so hard. And to really expand the potential ways that you can live as a human. That to me, the latter, is the interesting part.
turns.zh: 我觉得这甚至更广泛。我认为作为一个人，无论前 AI 时代还是后 AI 时代，你都有选择。你想消费还是创造？你想走容易的路还是想攀登高山？我现在看到很多的是人们让 AI 替他们思考。在 Figma 少一些，但在我与世界的互动中，我此刻看到很多这种情况。这是一条你可以走的路，但另一条是真正用 AI 来加深你对世界的理解，去学习，去做你以前不敢做的事情，因为那些事情要花太多时间去学或者太难了。并且真正扩展你作为人类生活的潜在方式。对我来说，后者才是有趣的部分。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: The former, like why would I want something else to think for me? Like my entire life has been about figuring out how to think. And I don't know, I just hope that people use AI to create good and to go be a force for it rather than just kind of joining the hive mind.
turns.zh: 前者，我为什么想让别的东西替我思考？我的一生都在琢磨如何思考。我不知道，我只是希望人们用 AI 来创造美好，成为一股力量，而不是仅仅加入蜂群思维。

turns.en: Everyone can be a maker.
turns.zh: 每个人都可以成为创造者。

turns.en: Everyone can be a maker. Everyone can go do both things. It's about willpower and it's about curiosity. And if you're curious and you're willing to do the work, I believe
turns.zh: 每个人都可以成为创造者。每个人都可以去做这两件事。这关乎意志力和好奇心。如果你好奇并且愿意付出努力，我相信

turns.en: your truth.
turns.zh: 你的真理。

turns.en: Yeah, exactly. And then I think that you can go do incredible things. We will probably see a vastly different setup in the future where things that we can't imagine are possible and things we take for granted are no longer in the realm of what humans do every day. How exactly that will look, I don't think either of us can tell. But it is the case that both were on the precipice of great change and nothing hit home for me more than the math drop last night from OpenAI of 700 plus papers on all sorts of very famous problems. That was a show of something. I had a lot of emotions. I don't know how to process them.
turns.zh: 没错，正是如此。然后我认为你可以去做不可思议的事情。未来我们可能会看到截然不同的格局，我们无法想象的事情成为可能，而我们习以为常的事情不再属于人类日常所做的范畴。具体会是什么样子，我想我们俩都说不准。但事实是，我们都处在巨大变革的边缘，而昨晚 OpenAI 发布的 700 多篇关于各种著名问题的数学论文，对我来说再震撼不过了。那展示了某种东西。我有很多情绪。我不知道如何处理它们。

turns.en: thought it was the greatest day of discovery in human history.
turns.zh: 我认为那是人类历史上最伟大的发现日。

turns.en: Oh, I mean, factually, yes.
turns.zh: 哦，我是说，事实上，是的。

turns.en: Yes. And also like something about it was like brilliant and exciting and something about it was kind of sad.
turns.zh: 是的。而且它有些方面是辉煌而激动人心的，有些方面又有点悲伤。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And I don't know how to articulate the sadness, but it felt like we lost something and gained something at the same time.
turns.zh: 我不知道如何表达这种悲伤，但感觉我们同时失去了一些东西，也得到了一些东西。

turns.en: I know. I lift my head up and I look at the next frontier and I think that the frontiers are brighter and wider and more accessible than they've ever been. So, I'm pretty excited.
turns.zh: 我知道。我抬起头，看向下一个前沿，我认为这些前沿比以往任何时候都更明亮、更广阔、更易触及。所以，我相当兴奋。

turns.en: Oh, I'm excited, too. And I think that the world will look amazing and I'm an optimist. I think there's going to be a lot of challenges and we'll figure them out.
turns.zh: 哦，我也很兴奋。我认为世界会看起来很棒，我是个乐观主义者。我认为会有很多挑战，我们会解决它们。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: How exactly and what the challenges will be in their full form, we have yet to see. But yeah, I do think that math is something that somehow has a quality of mystery like an unsolved problem. Is it, you know, is this conjecture true or false? How? Why? Grappling with that mystery is something that is special. And I'm both excited for the progress and all the things it'll make possible. And also I don't think it's wrong to mourn the loss of a little mystery.
turns.zh: 具体如何以及挑战的完整形态，我们还未看到。但没错，我确实认为数学有某种神秘的特质，就像一个未解决的问题。你知道，这个猜想是真的还是假的？如何？为什么？与那种神秘搏斗是件特别的事情。我既对进步和它将使一切成为可能感到兴奋，也认为为失去一点神秘而哀悼并没有错。

turns.en: Right. Fair enough. Dylan, this has been a great chat. Should we go over another drink?
turns.zh: 对。说得对。Dylan，这是一次很棒的聊天。我们再去喝一杯吧？

turns.en: Sounds good.
turns.zh: 听起来不错。

turns.en: Let's do it.
turns.zh: 走吧。

turns.en: Thanks, man.
turns.zh: 谢谢，伙计。

turns.en: Thanks.
turns.zh: 谢谢。

turns.en: I'm going all in. I'm going all in.
turns.zh: 我全力以赴。我全力以赴。

tldr.en: Design is the new code; as coding models improve, differentiation shifts to design, brand, and point of view.
tldr.zh: 设计即新代码；随着编码模型进步，差异化转向设计、品牌和观点。

tldr.en: AI lowers the floor for production but does not raise the ceiling; humans raise the ceiling through bold creativity.
tldr.zh: AI 降低了生产门槛，但并未提高上限；人类通过大胆创意提高上限。

tldr.en: In the attention economy, only truly novel and bold work breaks through; AI-generated average output gets ignored.
tldr.zh: 在注意力经济中，只有真正新颖大胆的作品才能突破；AI 生成的普通输出会被忽视。
